captions.instagram:
How does a fridge magnet work?

The back of a fridge magnet is not one pole but hundreds of thin stripes, turned so that all the field comes out of one side. See the real field lines, feel why two magnets jump in steps, and run a load test to find what actually holds your shopping list up: friction.

→ A fridge magnet is a picture on a thin sheet of rubber packed with ferrite powder.
→ Its back is not one pole. It is stripes, north, south, north, south, each about 2 mm wide.
→ Turn the magnetism round in steps and the field piles up on the back and almost vanishes from the front.
→ Slide two fridge magnets back to back and they jump in steps: stripes attracting, then repelling.
→ The steel door becomes a mirror image of the stripes, and the field lines dive straight into it.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/fridgemagnetclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a fridge magnet work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
The back of a fridge magnet is not one pole but hundreds of thin stripes, turned so that all the field comes out of one side. See the real field lines, feel why two magnets jump in steps, and run a load test to find what actually holds your shopping list up: friction.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/fridgemagnetclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/fridgemagnetclear

In this video:
• Rubber packed with ferrite powder. A flat fridge magnet is a printed picture on a dark sheet less than a millimetre thick.
• Stripes that turn: the one-sided trick. The back is not one north pole.
• You can feel and see the stripes. Slide two fridge magnets back to back and they jump along in steps of about 4 mm, as the stripes attract, repel and attract again.
• The steel door becomes a mirror magnet. A fridge door is painted steel.
• Friction does the lifting. The magnet pulls into the door, not upwards.
• Hard magnets reach further. A ceramic or neodymium disc has one pole on each face, so its field reaches centimetres instead of millimetres.
